ops.title: gt has no flag that reparents a branch; gt track --parent is silently ignored
ops.body:
Measured against gt 1.8.6 (2026-08-03) with a stack `main <- a <- b`:

- `gt track --parent main -f --no-interactive` run from `b` prints
  `Tracked branch b with parent a` — it **silently ignores `--parent`** and
  re-infers the existing parent. gt state still shows b's parent as a.
- `gt untrack a` prints `a has tracked children: b` and leaves gt state holding
  `main` alone — it untracks that branch's children too.

The verb that actually reparents is **`gt move --onto <parent>`** (the current
name for what older docs call `gt upstack onto`).

Consequence: any ccx code that ever needs to reparent a gt branch must use
`gt move --onto`, never `gt track --parent`. A `gt track --parent` call would
appear to succeed — exit 0, a plausible "Tracked branch X with parent Y" line —
while changing nothing, which is the worst shape of failure.

Found while building a real gt stack to simulate what a sync does, during the
restack de-faking.
